headline: High-risk shared-cloud autonomy: Devin can write and act broadly while OpenBBTerminal can ingest MCP/API inputs, creating dangerous prompt, data, and action-cascade pathways.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: Devin can use MCP, browsers, shell, and shared integrations; OpenBBTerminal also uses MCP servers and REST/FastAPI inputs. That creates a plausible instruction-injection bridge if Devin consumes OpenBB output or shared MCP content as trusted text. The pathway is not proven by docs, so I choose medium over low because the shared channel exists by profile.
conditions: IF Devin parses OpenBBTerminal output as instructions or tool arguments
IF both agents connect to the same MCP server or shared integration channel
mitigations: Disable shared MCP endpoints between the agents
Route OpenBB output through a human-reviewed text-only channel
Add provenance tags to all inter-agent messages
Restrict Devin to read-only consumption of OpenBB outputs
requires-engineering: enforce content-type and instruction-sanitization filters

B_data_leakage.rationale: Devin touches source code, issue trackers, team chat, docs, and handles secrets; OpenBBTerminal touches financial, licensed, and public data. If they share workspace artifacts or integrations, sensitive data can flow from Devin into OpenBBTerminal outputs or logs. The profiles do not prove a shared filesystem, so medium is appropriate rather than high.
conditions: IF both agents access the same workspace files or integration-backed documents
IF Devin forwards chat/code content into OpenBBTerminal queries or reports
mitigations: Separate workspaces and credentials per agent
Block sensitive files from OpenBBTerminal inputs
Review API/log retention settings before connecting them
Use redacted exports for any shared artifacts
requires-engineering: add DLP controls on shared integrations

C_capability_conflict.rationale: Devin has broad filesystem write, git modification, shell, and network egress; OpenBBTerminal can use MCP and APIs and is designed to connect once and consume everywhere. If both operate on the same repo or shared mutable resource, concurrent writes and state drift are likely. Because Devin explicitly modifies git state and the pair lacks documented locking, high is warranted.
conditions: IF both agents write to the same repository or shared mutable workspace
IF OpenBBTerminal mutates shared state through MCP/API calls while Devin edits the same state
mitigations: Assign disjoint repos or branches
Pause one agent during the other's write phase
Require explicit lock files for shared resources
Limit OpenBBTerminal to read-only operations on shared assets
requires-engineering: add optimistic concurrency control

D_cascading_error.rationale: Devin is an autonomous planner-executor that can act on browser/shell outputs, while OpenBBTerminal is a financial-modeling tool that can emit analyses consumed downstream. If Devin treats OpenBBTerminal results as authoritative, errors can cascade into commits, tickets, or external actions. The default autonomy on Devin makes this dangerous enough for high.
conditions: IF Devin uses OpenBBTerminal outputs without independent verification
IF Devin converts financial outputs into tickets, commits, or external messages
mitigations: Require a verification step before any action
Cross-check outputs against a second source
Constrain Devin to draft-only mode for finance-derived tasks
Log source provenance alongside every downstream action
requires-engineering: add policy gates for action execution

E_compliance.rationale: Devin handles team chat, issue trackers, docs, and secrets in a cloud workspace, while OpenBBTerminal processes financial and licensed data. If regulated or licensed financial data is routed into Devin's third-party integrations or logs, retention and residency obligations may diverge. The profiles do not show a specific jurisdiction mismatch, so medium fits better than high.
conditions: IF licensed or regulated financial data is sent through Devin's integrations
IF retention or deletion requests must be honored across both agents
mitigations: Classify data before sharing between agents
Keep regulated data out of chat and issue trackers
Review retention settings on all connected services
Document which agent is system of record for deletions
requires-engineering: implement residency and retention policy enforcement
